title: Buddy Petit in his band and his death
summary: Buddy Petit played second trumpet with him and died on a July 4th; Milton went for him that morning.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Okay. Do you remember some of your other jobs or other bands you played in after after that Melenberg job then? Well I mean I had several bands because I mean on

a little before Buddy Petit. Buddy Petit was playing with me too. He worked with me too. Oh and in your band then? That's right. He was playing second trumpet with me. Buddy Petit. When he died Buddy Petit died on the 4th of July. That he was supposed to go away with me that morning. When I went to his house he was dying. Alright. That's Sunday. That's Sunday. The 4th of July. No he was sick I mean but not he thought he would have been able to make it. When I went there that morning he was dying. When we come back he was late.

Lil' Lawrence Toker. Toker. Well he was playing second with me when he died. He was playing my band when he died. He died on the 4th of July. Here in town? Right. Right there. Right on St. Claude and St. Philip.
Do you remember when he died of? What his trouble was? No I know. I never got to know him. I just wondered.

I know he had high fever. I mean when we went there that morning he was just talking about his aid. I mean he wanted to get up. He told his wife, I got to go with that man. I got his deposit. I got to go look like I can see him. I mean when we come back he was late. Because we played the 4th, 5th and 6th of July in Bures. Went to Boerwood for him. Coming back we stopped at Venus. Just less jobs like Bures. Well we took this fella. I don't know if you remember him. He used to call him Jamaica fella. He called him Trap. But he had to rush and get him right away. Trap plates. About stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff stuff like stuff stuff like stuff stuff stuff like stuff stuff
Yeah, the Jamaica fella. I had to run and get him that morning.
He used to play outdoor halls, and that was Shining Hill.
